Predicates:
Cost(x, y) ::: x costs y to take the GRE test.
Cheaper(y, z) ::: y is cheaper than z.
ProvidesFinancialAid(x, y) ::: x provides financial aid to y.
ProveHardship(x) ::: x proves economic hardship.
LivesInSingleParentFamily(x) ::: x lives in a single-parent family.
HasFewResources(x) ::: x has few resources available.
Applicant(x) ::: x is applying to take the GRE test.
Premises:
Cost(GRE, 205) ∧ Cheaper(205, 300) ::: It costs $205 to take the GRE test, which is cheaper than $300.
∀x (ProveHardship(x) → (LivesInSingleParentFamily(x) ∨ HasFewResources(x))) ::: Those living in single-parent families or with few resources can prove economic hardship.
LivesInSingleParentFamily(tom) ∧ HasFewResources(tom) ::: Tom lives in a single-parent family and has few resources.
Applicant(tom) ::: Tom is applying to take the GRE test.
Conclusion:
Cost(GRE, y) ∧ Cheaper(y, 300) ::: It costs below US $300 to take the GRE test.
